content:
Hi all, I wonder what is the reason for presence of both theorems and lemmas to communicate intent but the lack of corollaries? If lemmas are minor results (prerequisites) meant to build up to a theorem as a major result then why not also have a corollary alias already provided by Mathlib for minor results (consequences) that follow from a theorem?

Note I would not have wondered about this if Mathlib only provides theorems but as it also provides lemmas clearly the Mathlib maintainers had in mind to add "communication layer" on top. My question thus is why is the same communication layer incomplete, yet nonzero.
See also #mathlib4 > lemma vs theorem
Ok so the choice of lemmas was somewhat arbitrary then and is planned for removal. Thanks for the pointer, I mostly searched for previous conversations with the keyword "corollary"
i don't recall such a decision was made there? could you link to where you read that?

I thought messages like

Now that we're in a position where mathport has replaced every lemma with theorem; should we just remove the lemma keyword?

in

#mathlib4 > lemma vs theorem @ 💬

are from maintainers or people indicating projects are already replacing every lemma with theorem. I guess I was wrong then?
No conclusion to that particular question has been decided
I assume then no one would want to talk for at least providing a more complete set of lemma + theorem + corollary considering people are even discussing about whether to keep lemmas around.
Isn't it possible with metaprogramming to include one's own version? I would like to see such a template, since I could use some synonyms for lemma and corollary to make my lean code more readable.

J. J. Issai (project started by GRP) said:

Isn't it possible with metaprogramming to include one's own version? I would like to see such a template, since I could use some synonyms for lemma and corollary to make my lean code more readable.

To make this even easier on you, the following code add-on works for me:

/-- `corollary` means the same as `theorem` but is used to denote secondary results -/
syntax (name := corollary) declModifiers
  group("corollary " declId ppIndent(declSig) declVal) : command

/-- Implementation of the `corollary` command, by macro expansion to `theorem`. -/
@[macro «corollary»] meta def expandCorollary : Macro := fun stx =>
  -- Not using a macro match, to be more resilient against changes to `corollary`.
  -- This implementation ensures that any future changes to `theorem` are reflected in `corollary`
  let stx := stx.modifyArg 1 fun stx =>
    let stx := stx.modifyArg 0 (mkAtomFrom · "theorem" (canonical := true))
    stx.setKind ``Parser.Command.theorem
  pure <| stx.setKind ``Parser.Command.declaration

However I think we are all aware of the possibility to implement our own extensions, I was rather curious about the intent behind Mathlib and why it is simply not available there or eventually shouldn't be (but not the current situation that is stuck in-between).
